title: Historically important spaceflight trajectories
important_limit: Paths with confidence B or lower are educational reconstructions, not navigation products.

missions.title: Apollo 11
missions.vehicle: Saturn V; CSM Columbia; LM Eagle
missions.description: First human landing on the Moon; Armstrong and Aldrin landed in Mare Tranquillitatis while Collins remained in lunar orbit.
missions.why_famous: The first humans to land and walk on another world.
missions.trajectory_method: Mission-event reconstruction with Moon motion sampled from JPL, 30 representative CSM lunar orbits between NASA's insertion and departure times; not onboard telemetry or the LM descent.

missions.title: Vostok 1
missions.description: Yuri Gagarin completed one Earth orbit and landed by parachute near Engels.
missions.why_famous: First human in space and first human to orbit Earth.
missions.trajectory_method: Representative inclined orbit through the launch site, with estimated ascent and reentry constrained to the published landing area.

missions.title: Sputnik 1
missions.description: The first artificial satellite orbited Earth every roughly 96 minutes.
missions.why_famous: Its launch began the Space Age.
missions.trajectory_method: Three representative initial revolutions from published perigee, apogee and inclination; orbital decay is not modeled.

missions.title: Apollo 8
missions.description: The first crewed flight to the Moon and first human lunar orbit.
missions.why_famous: Its crew saw the lunar farside and made the iconic Earthrise photograph.
missions.trajectory_method: Mission-event reconstruction with Moon motion sampled from JPL and ten representative lunar orbits between NASA's insertion and departure times.

missions.title: Apollo 13
missions.vehicle: Saturn V; CSM Odyssey; LM Aquarius
missions.description: An oxygen-tank explosion forced an aborted landing and a life-saving loop around the Moon.
missions.why_famous: A defining spacecraft emergency and rescue, remembered as a successful failure.
missions.trajectory_method: Free-return style event reconstruction tied to moving Moon ephemeris, NASA's 1,988.8 km perilune radius and documented launch/splashdown times; flyby orientation is illustrative.

missions.title: Voyager 2
missions.description: Gravity assists carried Voyager 2 past Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune and onward into interstellar space.
missions.why_famous: The only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune, and all four giant planets.
missions.trajectory_method: Modeled east-southeast ascent and roughly 43-minute parking-orbit coast from NASA launch records; JPL Horizons spacecraft ephemeris sampled every minute from 15:32 UTC on launch day, then every five days. The pre-ephemeris arc is illustrative, not telemetry.

missions.title: STS-1 Columbia
missions.description: The first orbital test of the reusable Space Transportation System completed 37 revolutions.
missions.why_famous: First Space Shuttle mission and first crewed maiden flight of a U.S. spacecraft system.
missions.trajectory_method: Representative inclined orbit at published altitude, with estimated ascent and final 60-minute deorbit/entry arc constrained to Edwards AFB; not Shuttle telemetry.

missions.title: Friendship 7
missions.description: John Glenn became the first American to orbit Earth, completing three revolutions.
missions.why_famous: A central early U.S. Space Race achievement.
missions.trajectory_method: Representative inclined orbit using published duration and Mercury inclination, with estimated ascent/reentry ending at documented splashdown.

missions.title: Vostok 6
missions.description: Valentina Tereshkova completed 48 Earth orbits over almost three days.
missions.why_famous: First spaceflight by a woman.
missions.trajectory_method: Representative inclined orbit from published dimensions and duration, with estimated ascent/reentry ending at the landing region.

missions.title: Voyager 1
missions.description: Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter and Saturn/Titan before leaving the ecliptic and crossing the heliopause.
missions.why_famous: The most distant human-made object and first spacecraft in interstellar space.
missions.trajectory_method: JPL Horizons trajectory; early segment is documented by Horizons as a patched-conic reconstruction and later segment is tracking-data fitted.

missions.title: Cassini-Huygens
missions.description: Cassini used four planetary gravity assists to reach Saturn, while Huygens landed on Titan.
missions.why_famous: The definitive Saturn mission and first landing in the outer Solar System.
missions.trajectory_method: JPL Horizons Cassini ephemeris sampled every five days; separate Huygens descent is not represented in this overview path.

missions.title: New Horizons
missions.description: New Horizons used Jupiter to reach Pluto, then continued to Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth.
missions.why_famous: First close exploration of Pluto and the most distant close flyby ever conducted.
missions.trajectory_method: JPL Horizons mission ephemeris sampled every four days.

missions.title: Explorer 1
missions.description: The first U.S. satellite carried the instrument that discovered the Van Allen radiation belts.
missions.why_famous: It brought the United States into orbital spaceflight and made a foundational discovery.
missions.trajectory_method: Three representative initial revolutions from published perigee, apogee and inclination; long-term perturbation and decay are omitted.

missions.title: Viking 1
missions.description: Viking 1 entered Mars orbit and delivered the first fully successful long-lived Mars lander.
missions.why_famous: It returned the first enduring surface investigation and images from Mars.
missions.trajectory_method: Heliocentric transfer reconstruction between JPL Earth and Mars ephemerides; the curve is not the spacecraft's navigation solution.

missions.title: Mariner 4
missions.description: Mariner 4 performed the first successful Mars flyby and returned the first close images of another planet.
missions.why_famous: It replaced speculation about Mars with direct close-range observations.
missions.trajectory_method: Heliocentric transfer reconstruction between JPL Earth and Mars ephemerides; encounter position is planet-centred and not offset by the 9,846 km flyby distance.

missions.title: Luna 2
missions.description: The Soviet probe followed a direct translunar path and impacted the Moon.
missions.why_famous: First human-made object to reach another celestial body.
missions.trajectory_method: One-way mission-event reconstruction terminating on the approximate lunar near-side surface at the Moon's JPL ephemeris position; exact impact coordinates are not resolved.

missions.title: Venera 7
missions.description: Venera 7 survived its descent through Venus's atmosphere and returned surface data.
missions.why_famous: First successful transmission from the surface of another planet.
missions.trajectory_method: Heliocentric transfer reconstruction between JPL Earth and Venus ephemerides; exact landing coordinates are unknown and not invented.

missions.title: Apollo-Soyuz Test Project
missions.description: American and Soviet spacecraft launched separately, rendezvoused and docked in Earth orbit.
missions.why_famous: The first international crewed spaceflight and an enduring symbol of Cold War cooperation.
missions.trajectory_method: Representative Apollo docking orbit from published altitude and inclination with estimated ascent/reentry; Soyuz phasing is not separately resolved.

missions.title: Soyuz 11 and Salyut 1
missions.description: Soyuz 11 carried the first crew to live aboard a space station; all three cosmonauts died during return depressurization.
missions.why_famous: It established the crewed-space-station model and remains a defining spaceflight tragedy.
missions.trajectory_method: Representative Salyut-class orbit and mission duration with estimated ascent/reentry; rendezvous and station-keeping burns are not reconstructed.

missions.title: Rosetta and Philae
missions.description: Rosetta used repeated Earth and Mars assists to rendezvous with comet 67P; Philae landed on its nucleus.
missions.why_famous: First spacecraft to rendezvous with and escort a comet, and first comet landing.
missions.trajectory_method: JPL Horizons/ESA mission ephemeris sampled every two days; Philae's local descent and bounces are not represented.

missions.title: Mars Science Laboratory / Curiosity
missions.description: The Mars Science Laboratory carried Curiosity to Gale Crater and delivered it with the sky-crane system.
missions.why_famous: The seven-minutes-of-terror landing became a modern spaceflight landmark.
missions.trajectory_method: JPL Horizons spacecraft ephemeris sampled every twelve hours; atmospheric descent and surface traverse are separate local datasets not included here.

missions.title: Hayabusa2
missions.description: Hayabusa2 rendezvoused with asteroid Ryugu, sampled it, and returned a capsule to Australia.
missions.why_famous: First return of subsurface asteroid material.
missions.trajectory_method: JPL Horizons mission ephemeris sampled daily; the final sample-capsule atmospheric branch is not separately resolved.

missions.title: Shenzhou 5
missions.description: Yang Liwei completed 14 Earth orbits and landed in Inner Mongolia.
missions.why_famous: Made China the third nation to independently launch and return a human from orbit.
missions.trajectory_method: Representative inclined orbit using CMSA's published insertion/circularization data, with estimated ascent/reentry to the landing region.

missions.title: Artemis I
missions.description: The first integrated SLS-Orion flight completed lunar flybys and a distant retrograde lunar orbit.
missions.why_famous: Opened NASA's Artemis lunar campaign and tested the human-rated lunar-return system.
missions.trajectory_method: JPL Horizons Orion ephemeris sampled every two hours.

missions.title: Chandrayaan-3
missions.description: Chandrayaan-3 raised its Earth orbit, transferred to lunar polar orbit, and landed Vikram in the Moon's southern high latitudes.
missions.why_famous: Made India the fourth nation to soft-land on the Moon and first in the lunar south-polar region.
missions.trajectory_method: JPL Horizons Chandrayaan-3 propulsion-module ephemeris sampled every five minutes to resolve its eccentric Earth orbits. The first 17 minutes of ascent are modeled between the launch site and first available state; the lander descent is not part of this path.
